description: CompressionMultiHeadLUT with n_heads=3, INDEPENDENT per-head (joint_head_compression=False), inner_in_dim=inner_out_dim=64 (via inner_dim=64), NO inner residual, NAP=6, hard. PARAMETER-MATCHED to exp032 (35,792,640). FFN slot fully replaced: x = x + compressionmhl(ln2(x)). Independent per-head means: compress = one Linear(384 -> 3*64=192) whose 3 row-blocks are the per-head compress maps; each head runs its OWN single-head FastMHL(64->64) on its own 64-d slice; decompress = one Linear(3*64=192 -> 384) over the concatenated per-head outputs (== summed per-head decompress). This is a param-matched A/B against exp041 (inner=192, single head): SAME total params and same 192-wide inner budget, but split block-diagonally into 3 independent 64-d heads vs one 192-d head -- does per-head routing beat one wide head? PARAM MATCH: fixed compress(384*192+192=73,920)+decompress(192*384+384=74,112)=148,032/layer; FastMHL budget 1,179,648-148,032=1,031,616 -> tph = 1,031,616/(3*2^6*64)=83.95 -> tph=84 -> FastMHL 3*84*64*64=1,032,192; per-layer 1,180,224 (~=FFN 1,179,648, +576); total 35,796,096, delta +3,456 = +0.0097%. Byte-identical to the rest of the sweep otherwise (MinimalGPT+RoPE d384/6L/6H/seq512, device_bs 48, total_bs 24576, n_steps 4096, lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, warmup 0.1, eval_every 200, seed 1, vocab 32768, same data). Optimizer: LUT tables no-wd; compress/decompress weight wd, bias no-wd. Compare vs exp040 inner128 1.39903 (best), exp041 inner192 1.40936, exp036 inner64 1.40699.
